findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator treats the `datetime` key as a number, so the optimized audit-log path crashes.
findings.body: The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`, and `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key` on every non-empty page. As a result, every request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns rows fails with a 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw cursor number, so `build_queryset` compares a datetime column with an int or float. The fix is to reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s key and cursor conversion, for example by subclassing `DateTimePaginator` instead of `BasePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed directly into a Django queryset slice.
findings.body: Django querysets reject negative indexing ("Negative indexing is not supported."). A client-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:0` reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start, and the request fails with a 500. The comment saying the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" is wrong. If it did work, its stated purpose is to reach "data beyond normal pagination bounds". The comment's claim that this is "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is unsupported and reads as reassurance aimed at reviewers. The fix is to clamp the offset to `max(0, offset)` or reject negative offsets when parsing the cursor. The `else` branch at line 884 has the same problem when `is_prev` is set.

findings.title: The gate checks the raw `is_superuser` flag instead of an active superuser session.
findings.body: `request.user.is_superuser` is true for any superuser account even without an active, verified superuser session. Elsewhere Sentry uses `is_active_superuser(request)` to enforce sudo/SSO for superuser privileges. Using the flag lets a superuser account without an elevated session turn on the 'advanced' paginator. The fix is to use `is_active_superuser(request)`. I could not confirm from these hunks that `organization_context.member` is always non-None for non-superusers; if it can be None, `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`.

findings.title: This changes offset handling in the shared BasePaginator, which every endpoint uses.
findings.body: This edit changes slicing for every BasePaginator subclass across the API, not only audit logs. A negative offset on a forward cursor used to error and is now silently clamped to 0. A negative offset on a prev cursor still goes to the queryset and crashes. The comment says negative offsets are "safe", which is wrong. The audit-log request does not call for changing this shared code path. The fix is to revert it, or to reject negative offsets consistently in both directions.
